# Spillway regulation below the main dam

The dam's spillway gates do not generate power and were not built to; their entire function is to control how much water is released downstream per hour, independent of how much water is arriving from upstream at any given moment. During a heavy rain event, inflow can spike far above what the downstream channel and the towns along it could safely absorb all at once, and the gates hold most of that spike back in the reservoir, releasing it gradually over the following days instead.

The engineer managing the gates described the job, in a recent report, as having almost nothing to do with the water itself and everything to do with the rate: the reservoir can absorb a huge volume over time that the downstream channel could never absorb in an hour, so the gates exist purely to convert a dangerous spike in the rate of delivery into a manageable, sustained rate the downstream infrastructure can actually handle without flooding, protecting a capacity that has a hard ceiling regardless of how much total water needs to eventually pass through it.
